task_instance: Using the Plotly Python library, take a small sample scientific CSV (temperature vs yield across batches) and produce an interactive scatter plot with an OLS trendline exported to a standalone interactive HTML file (chart.html), as the skill's Quick Start and Scientific Data Visualization workflow describe.
blocker_detail: The skill is the Plotly Python graphing library. Its core deliverable (a plotly Figure exported to interactive HTML, or to a static PNG/PDF/SVG via kaleido) can only be produced by installing plotly (uv pip install plotly) and executing a Python script that builds the figure and calls fig.write_html / fig.write_image. The office-assistant runtime cannot run code or shell commands of any kind and cannot install software, so the figure cannot be built or exported. I wrote the input data and the exact plotly script as text, but there is no way to execute it or verify a rendered chart. Writing a hand-authored plotly.js HTML page instead would be a self-made replacement for the Python SDK, which the run rules forbid.
evidence: Read skill at components/skills/scientific/plotly/SKILL.md (Quick Start installs via 'uv pip install plotly' and runs Python: px.scatter(...); fig.write_html(...); static export needs kaleido and fig.write_image). Created input sample_data.csv (10 rows: temperature,yield,batch) and make_chart.py (plotly express scatter with trendline='ols' -> write_html) in the work directory. The script was not and cannot be executed in this runtime (no code execution), so no chart.html was produced and the deliverable could not be verified.
